questions.q: A point charge of $+ 12\muC$ is at a distance $6$ cm vertically above the centre of a square of side $12$ cm as shown in figure. The magnitude of the electric flux through the square will be _______~$\times {10}^{3}Nm^{2}C^{- 1} .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From symmetry& $ϕ = \dfrac{1}{6} \left(\dfrac{q}{ε0}\right)

$= $\dfrac{12 \times {10}^{- 6}}{6 \times 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}}

$= 225 . 98 $\times {10}^{3}$Nm^{2}C^{- 1}≃ 226 $\times {10}^{3}$Nm^{2}C^{- 1}$

$

questions.q:
As shown in the figure, a configuration of two equal point charges \left({q}_{0} = + 2\muC\right)$ is placed on an inclined plane. Mass of each point charge is $20g$. Assume that there is no friction between charge and plane. For the system of two point charges to be in equilibrium (at rest) the height $h = x \times {10}^{- 3}m$. The value of$x$~is
\left(\text{Take}\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{2}C^{- 2}, g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the condition of equilibrium, the Coulomb force is equal to& $mgsin\theta$. Hence,

$\dfrac{k{q0}^{2}}{4h^{2}} = ( mgsin\theta ) ⇒ \dfrac{k{q0}^{2}}{4h^{2}} = \left(20 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times 4 \times {10}^{- 12}}{4h^{2}} = 20 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ h = \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{100}}\right)m = 0 . 3m = 300 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

$h^{2} = \left(\dfrac{9}{100}\right) ⇒ h = \left(\dfrac{3}{10}\right)m = 0 .3 m$

$= 300 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

questions.q: An infinite plane sheet of charge having uniform surface charge density $+\sigma_s \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^2$ is placed on $x-y$ plane. Another infinitely long line charge having uniform linear charge density $+\lambda_e \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}$ is placed at $z=4 \mathrm{~m}$ plane and parallel to $y$-axis. If the magnitude values \left|\sigma_{\mathrm{s}}\right|=2\left|\lambda_{\mathrm{e}}\right|$ then at point $(0,0,2)$, the ratio of magnitudes of electric field values due to sheet charge to that of line charge is $\pi \sqrt{n}: 1$. The value of $n$ is_______.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S}}}{\mathrm{E}_{\ell}}=\frac{\sigma}{2 \epsilon_0} \times \frac{2 \pi \epsilon_0 \mathrm{r}}{\lambda} \\ & =\frac{\pi \times \sigma \mathrm{r}}{\lambda} \\ & =\frac{\pi \times 2 \lambda \times 2}{\lambda}=\frac{4 \pi}{1} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{n}=16\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
For a charged spherical ball, electrostatic potential inside the ball varies with $r$ as~$V = 2ar^{2} + b$.

Here, $a$ and $b$ are constant and $r$ is the distance from the center. The volume charge density inside the ball is $- \lambdaaε$. The value of $\lambda$ is ______.

$ε =$& permittivity of medium.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,& $E = - \dfrac{dV}{dr} = - 4ar$

Now, electric field inside the charged sphere is given by $E = \dfrac{ρr}{3ε}$.~

Comparing both, we get~$ρ = - 12aε$.

Therefore,~$\lambda = 12$.

questions.q:
If the net electric field at point $\mathrm{P}$ along $\mathrm{Y}$ axis is zero, then the ratio of \left|\frac{q_2}{q_3}\right|$ is $\frac{8}{5 \sqrt{x}}$, where $x=$ _____.
$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{Kq}_2}{20} \cos \beta=\frac{\mathrm{Kq}_3}{25} \cos \theta \\ & \frac{\mathrm{Kq}_2}{20} \frac{4}{\sqrt{20}}=\frac{\mathrm{Kq}_3}{25} \frac{4}{\sqrt{25}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{q}_3}=\frac{20}{25} \sqrt{\frac{20}{25}}=\frac{8}{5 \sqrt{\mathrm{x}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{x}}=\frac{8 \times 25 \sqrt{25}}{5 \times 20 \sqrt{20}} \\ & \mathrm{x}=5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The total charge enclosed in an incremental volume of $2 \times {10}^{- 9}m^{3}$ located at the origin is~ $nC,$~if electric flux density of its field is found as$D = e^{- x}siny\overset{^}{i} - e^{- x}cosy\overset{^}{j} + 2z\overset{^}{k}Cm^{- 2}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric flux density,

\left(\overset{→}{D}\right) = \dfrac{\text{charge}}{\text{Area}} \times \overset{^}{r} = \dfrac{Q}{4\pir^{2}}\overset{^}{r} = {ϵ}_{0} \left(\dfrac{Q}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}r^{2}}\overset{^}{r}\right)

$⇒ \overset{→}{E} = \overset{→}{D}{ϵ}_{0} = $\dfrac{e^{- x}siny\overset{^}{i} - e^{- x}cos ( \overset{^}{j} + 2z\overset{^}{k )}}{ϵ0}

Also, by Gauss's law,

\dfrac{ρ}{ϵ0} = \left(\dfrac{∂}{∂ x}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{∂}{∂ y}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{∂}{∂ z}\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{E} = \left(\dfrac{∂}{∂ x}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{∂}{∂ y}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{∂}{∂ z}\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{D}{ϵ}_{0}

$⇒ ρ = $\dfrac{∂}{∂ x}\left($e^{- x}siny\right) + $\dfrac{∂}{∂ y}\left(-$e^{- x}cosy\right) + $\dfrac{∂}{∂ z} ($2z )$

$ρ = - e^{- x}siny + e^{- x}siny + 2$
At origin~$ρ = - e^{- 0}sin0 + e^{- 0}sin0 + 2$
$ρ = 2Cm^{- 3}$

Charge $= ρ $\times volume~$= 2 $\times$2 $\times {10}^{- 9} =$4 $\times {10}^{- 9} =
$4nC$

questions.q: Two identical charged spheres are suspended by strings of equal lengths. The string make an angle of $37 °$ with each other. When suspended in a liquid of density $0 . 7g{cm}^{- 3}$, the angle remains same. If density of material of the sphere is $1 . 4g{cm}^{- 3}$, the dielectric constant of the liquid is _____  \left(tan37 ° = \dfrac{3}{4}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For first case:

$Tcos\theta = mg$ and

$Tsin\theta = {F}_{e}$

Therefore, $tan\theta = \dfrac{Fe}{mg}$

$tan\theta = \dfrac{Fe}{{ρ}_{B}Vg} . . . . ( i )$

For second case:

$tan\theta = \dfrac{{F}_{e}k}{{ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{L}Vg} . . . . . ( ii )$

From Eq. (i) & (ii), we get

${ρ}_{B}Vg = \left({ρ}_{B} - {ρ}_{L}\right)kVg$

$⇒ 1 . 4 = 0 . 7k$

$⇒ k = 2$

questions.q: Three concentric spherical metallic shells $X, Y$ and $Z$ of radius $a, b$ and $c$ respectively~  \left[a < b < c\right]$ have surface charge densities $\sigma, – \sigma$ and $\sigma$, respectively. The shells $X$ and $Z$ are at same potential. If the radii of $X \text{ and } Y$ are $2$ cm and $3$ cm, respectively. The radius of shell $Z$ is _____cm$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The charges on the spheres are

& ${q}_{X} = \sigma4\pia^{2}{q}_{Y} = - \sigma4\pib^{2}{q}_{Z} = \sigma4\pic^{2}$

It is given that~${V}_{X} = {V}_{Z}$

So,~

$\dfrac{qX}{4\pi{ε}_{0}a} + \dfrac{qY}{4\pi{ε}_{0}b} + \dfrac{{q}_{Z}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}c} = \dfrac{{q}_{X}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}c} + \dfrac{{q}_{Y}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}c} + \dfrac{{q}_{Z}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}c} ⇒ \dfrac{\sigma4\pia^{2}}{a} - \dfrac{\sigma4\pib^{2}}{b} + \dfrac{\sigma4\pic^{2}}{c} = \dfrac{\sigma4\pi ( a^{2} - b^{2} + c^{2} )}{c} ⇒ c ( a - b + c ) = ( a^{2} - b^{2} + c^{2} ) ⇒ c = a + b = 2cm + 3cm = 5cm$

questions.q: A stream of a positively charged particles having $\dfrac{q}{m} = 2 \times {10}^{11}C{kg}^{- 1}$ and velocity $\overset{→}{v}0 = 3 \times {10}^{7}\overset{^}{i}ms^{- 1}$ is deflected by an electric field $1 . 8\overset{^}{j}kVm^{- 1}$. The electric field exists in a region of $10$ cm along $x$ direction. Due to the electric field, the deflection of the charge particles in the $y$ direction is _____ $mm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration of the particles due to electric field,& $a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{qE}{m} = \left(2 \times {10}^{11}\right)\left($1 . 8 $\times {10}^{3}\right)

$= 3 . 6 $\times {10}^{14}$ms^{- 2}$

Time to cross plates $= $\dfrac{d}{v}

$⇒ t = $\dfrac{0 . 10}{3 \times {10}^{7}}

Now deflection,

$y = $\dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(3 . 6 \times {10}^{14}\right)\left(\dfrac{0 . 10}{3 \times {10}^{7}}\right)2$

$= 0 . 002m$

$= 2mm$

questions.q: The electric field in a region is given by $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \times 10^3 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{C}$. The flux of the field through a rectangular surface parallel to $x-z$ plane is $6.0 \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrmC^{-1}$. The area of the surface is ________ $\mathrm{cm}^2$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \phi=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \times 10^3 \cdot \mathrm{~A} \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ & 6=4 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \mathrm{~A}=1.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2 \\ & =15 \mathrm{~cm}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
An infinite number of point charges, each& carrying $1\muC$ charge, are placed along the y-axis at $y = 1m, 2m, 4m, 8m . . . .$

The total force on a $1C$ point charge, placed at the origin, is $x \times {10}^{3}N$. The value of $x$,~to~the nearest integer, is ___ .

[Take $\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{2}C^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$F = k \left(1C\right) \left($1\muC\right)\left[$1 + $\dfrac{1}{22} + \dfrac{1}{42} + \dfrac{1}{82} + \ldots\right]

$= 9 $\times {10}^{3}\$left[\dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}}\right] =12 $\times {10}^{3}$N$

$

questions.q:
A cubical volume is bounded by the surfaces $x = 0, x = a, y = 0, y = a, z = 0, z = a$. The electric field in the region is given by $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}x\overset{^}{i}$. Where ${E}_{0} = 4 \times {10}^{4}{NC}^{- 1}m^{- 1}$. If $a = 2cm$, the charge contained in the cubical volume is $Q \times {10}^{– 14}C$. The value of $Q$ is ______.

(Take~${ϵ}_{0} = 9 \times {10}^{- 12}C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, electric field,& $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}x\overset{^}{i}$

Here, the flux passes mainly through surface areas,~$ABCDandEFGH$. As the surfaces~$AEFBandCGHD$~are parallel~to the electric field, so flux for these surfaces are zero. Again in $EFGH$,~$a = 0$, thus, electric field is zero.

Hence, the flux only passes through the surface are $ABCD$.

The net flux is~${ϕ}_{net} = {ϕ}_{ABCD} = {E}_{0}a \cdot a^{2}$

Using~Gauss's law,~$\dfrac{qen}{ϵ0} = {E}_{0}a^{3}$

$⇒ {q}_{en} = {E}_{0}{ε}_{0}a^{3}$

$= 4 \times {10}^{4} \times 9 \times {10}^{- 12} \times 8 \times {10}^{- 6}$

$= 288 \times {10}^{- 14}C$

Hence, the value of~$Q = 288$.

questions.q:
As shown in figure, a cuboid lies in a region with electric field& $E = 2x^{2}\overset{^}{i} - 4y\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}NC^{- 1}$.~The magnitude of charge within the cuboid is~$n{ε}_{0}C$.

The value of $n$ is ______~(if dimension of cuboid is~$1 \times 2 \times 3m^{3}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\overset{→}{E} = 2x^{2}\overset{^}{i} - 4y\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

For top and bottom faces, as~value of~$x = 0 \text{ and } y = 0$, electric field becomes constant and therefore net flux through these two faces will be zero(${ϕ}_{z} = 0$).

Now,~${E}_{x} = 2x^{2}$,~${E}_{y} = - 4y$~and~${E}_{z} = 6$.

Change in net flux through face at x=1 and at x=0~parallel to y-z plane can written as,~${ϕ}_{x} = \left(2 \times {1}^{2}\right) \times \left(2 \times 3\right) - 0 = 12$.

Similarly, net flux through face at y=2 and y=0 parallel to x-z plane can be written as,~${ϕ}_{y} = - \left(4 \times 2\right) \times \left(1 \times 3\right) - 0 = - 24$

${ϕ}_{net} = 12 - 24 = - 12$

Using Gauss's law,

${ϕ}_{net} = \dfrac{q}{ε0}$

$⇒ \left|q\right| = 12{ε}_{0}$

questions.q: Three infinitely long charged thin sheets are placed as shown in figure. The magnitude of electric field at the point $P$ is $\frac{x \sigma}{\epsilon_o}$. The value of $x$ is _______ (all quantities are measured in SI units).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}_{\mathrm{p}} & =\left(\frac{\sigma}{2 \varepsilon_0}+\frac{2 \sigma}{2 \varepsilon_0}+\frac{\sigma}{2 \varepsilon_0}\right)(-\hat{\mathrm{i}}) \\ & =-\frac{2 \sigma}{\varepsilon_0} \hat{\mathrm{i}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The electric field in a region is given by& $\overset{→}{E} = \dfrac{2}{5}{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{3}{5}{E}_{0}\overset{^}{j}$ with ${E}_{0} = 4 . 0 \times {10}^{3}NC^{- 1} .$ The flux of this field through a rectangular surface, area $0 . 4m^{2}$ parallel to the $Y - Z$ plane is _______~$Nm^{2}C^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: Two small spheres each of mass $10$ mg are suspended from a point by threads $0 . 5m$ long. They are equally charged and repel each other to a distance of $0 . 20m$. The charge on each of~the sphere is $\dfrac{a}{21} \times {10}^{- 8}C .$~The value of $a$ will be ___.[Given $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
.

$Tcos\theta = mg = 10 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 10 = {10}^{- 4}$

$Tsin\theta = \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times q^{2}}{0 . 04} = F$

$tan\theta = = \dfrac{0 . 1}{0 . 24} = \dfrac{F}{mg}$

$q = \dfrac{2\sqrt{10}}{3\sqrt{\sqrt{24}}} \times {10}^{- 8}$

$0 . 95 \times {10}^{- 8} = \dfrac{a}{21} \times {10}^{- 8}$

$a = 20$

questions.q: Suppose a uniformly charged wall provides a uniform electric field of $2 \times {10}^{4}NC^{- 1}$ normally. A charged particle of mass $2g$ being suspended through a silk thread of length $20$ cm and remain stayed at a distance of $10$ cm from the wall. Then the charge on the particle will be $\dfrac{1}{x}\muC$ where $x =$ ________ [use $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we can see from geometry, $sin\theta = \dfrac{10}{20} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = 30 °$

Vertical component of tension will balance the weight and the horizontal component will balance the electric force. Therefore,

$tan\theta = \dfrac{qE}{mg}$

$⇒ tan30 ° = \dfrac{q \times 2 \times {10}^{4}}{2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 10}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3} = q \times {10}^{6}$

$⇒ q = \dfrac{1}{3} \times {10}^{- 6}C = \dfrac{1}{3}\mu C$

Hence, $x = 3$.

questions.q:
A thin metallic wire having cross sectional area of ${10}^{- 4}m^{2}$ is used to make a ring of radius $30$ cm. A positive charge of $2\piC$ is uniformly distributed over the ring, while another positive charge of $30pC$ is kept at the centre of the ring. The tension in the ring is _______N$; provided that the ring does not get deformed (neglect the influence of gravity).

(Given, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9} SI units)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The linear charge density of the ring is given by

$\lambda = \dfrac{Q}{2\piR} . . . \left(1\right)$

With reference to the above diagram, for the equilibrium condition of the ring, it can be written that

$2Tsin\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{q0}{R2} \cdot \left[\lambda \left(Rd\theta\right)\right]$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{{q}_{0}Q}{\left(R^{2}\right) \times 2\pi} [$As for very small angles $sin\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{d\theta}{2}]$

$= \dfrac{\left(9 \times {10}^{9}\right)\left(2\pi \times 30 \times {10}^{- 12}\right)}{( 0 . 30{)}^{2} \times 2\pi}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 30}{9 \times {10}^{- 2}} =3N$

questions.q: Two equal positive point charges are separated by a distance $2a$. The distance of a point from the centre of the line joining two charges on the equatorial line (perpendicular bisector) at which force experienced by a test charge ${q}_{0}$ becomes maximum is~$\dfrac{a}{x}$.~The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let us assume at distance& $y$, force is maximum.

Now, force at a distance~$y$~is given by,~${F}_{net} = 2Fcos\theta$

So,~${F}_{net} = \dfrac{2Kq{q}_{0}y}{\left(y^{2} + a^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}$

For ${F}_{net}$ to be maximum,~$\dfrac{d{F}_{net}}{dy} = 0$

Or~$Kq{q}_{0}\dfrac{\left(y^{2} + a^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - y\dfrac{3}{2} \times 2y\left(y^{2} + a^{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}}{\left(y^{2} + a^{2}\right)3} = 0$

Simplifying, we get~$y = \dfrac{a}{2}$.

Hence, the value of~$x = 2$.

questions.q: A uniform electric field of $10NC^{- 1}$ is created between two parallel charged plates (as shown in figure). An electron enters the field symmetrically between the plates with a kinetic energy $0 . 5eV .$ The length of each plate is $10$ cm. The angle $( \theta )$ of deviation of the path of electron as it comes out of the field is ______(in degree).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, kinetic energy& $\dfrac{1}{2}e = \dfrac{1}{2}m{u}_x^{2} ⇒ {u}_{x} = \sqrt{\dfrac{e}{m}}$

Acceleration of electron due to electric field is~$a = \dfrac{eE}{m}$, where,~$e$~is charge on electron.

Using equation of motion,~$s = {u}_{x}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{x}t^{2}$~ along~$x$~direction, we get

$L = {u}_{x}t + 0 \left(∵ {a}_{x} = 0\right) ⇒ 10 \times {10}^{- 2} = {u}_{x}t ⇒ t = $\dfrac{10- 1}{ux} . . . . \left($1\right)$

Using equation of motion, ${v}_{y} = {u}_{y} + {a}_{y}t$~along y direction, we get

${v}_{y} = 0 + $\dfrac{eE}{m}$t = $\dfrac{eE}{m}$t . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation \left(1\right)and \left(2\right)$, we have

${v}_{y} = $\dfrac{eE}{m} $\$left(\dfrac{10- 1}{ux}\right)

Now,~tan\theta = \dfrac{vy}{vx} = \dfrac{eE}{m}\left({10}^{- 1}{u}_x^{2}\right) = $\dfrac{e \times 10 \times {10}^{- 1}}{m \times \dfrac{e}{m}} =$1$

The angle of deviation of the path of electron as it comes out of the field is~\theta =$45 °$.

$
